text: From Leavenworth, drive US 2 west about 17.5 miles (or about 18 miles east from Stevens Pass) to just past the Nason Creek Rest Area and turn north onto the unsigned Butcher Creek Road, FR 6910; the turn is on a curve with fast traffic. Follow good gravel about 4.5 miles, then take spur FR 6910-170 a short way to the Round Mountain Trailhead at about 3,900 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

From US 2 about 0.6 mile east of milepost 33, roughly 2.5 miles east of Gold Bar, turn right (south) onto Forest Road 62. Follow it about 3.5 miles to the FR 6220 junction and bear left, go a little over a mile to a second junction and bear left again, then drive the last rough mile to a small pullout near the road end at about 2,800 ft. A Hampton Resources recreation permit is required, and a loc

pins.name: Smith Brook Road (FR 6700) — first major switchback, start of the Lichtenwasser Lake approach

text: In summer, drive US 2 to the Smith Brook Road turnoff, Forest Road 6700, roughly 3.5 to 4 miles east of Stevens Pass around mileposts 68.7 to 68.9. Follow the unpaved road up toward the Smithbrook Trailhead and park at or near the first major switchback, where the Lichtenwasser Lake fishing trail leads off toward the lake. In winter FR 6700 is unplowed, so park on the shoulder of US 2 at or just b

From Quilcene, drive US 101 south about 1.5 miles and turn right (west) onto Penny Creek Road. After about 1.5 miles bear left onto Big Quilcene River Road, FR 27, and follow it about 9.25 miles to FR 2750. Turn left and drive about 4.75 miles on this narrow, single-lane road to the Upper Big Quilcene Trailhead at its end, about 2,600 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is needed to park; no wilderness pe

In Chelan, follow SR 150 (E Woodin Ave), turn left on Sanders St, then left on Farnham St, continue onto S Saunders St, and turn left on E Iowa Ave to the trailhead parking lot on the left. A Discover Pass or WDFW Vehicle Access Pass is required to park.

From US 101 about 0.9 mile south of the Quilcene Ranger Station, bear right onto Penny Creek Road. In about 1.5 miles take the left fork onto Forest Road 27 and follow it about 12 miles, then turn left onto Forest Road 190 and follow it about a mile to its end at the upper trailhead, a small gravel lot at about 3,300 ft. No parking pass is required.

pins.name: Hoh River Trailhead (Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center)

text: From Forks, drive south on US 101 about 13 miles and turn east onto Upper Hoh Road. Follow it about 18 miles to its end at the Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center, where the Hoh River Trail begins. An Olympic National Park entrance pass is required, and overnight wilderness permits must be reserved in advance.

pins.name: Hoh River Trailhead (Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center)
Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center / Hoh River Trailhead
Hoh River Trailhead (Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center)

text: From US 101 about 13 miles south of Forks, turn east on Upper Hoh Road and drive about 18 miles to the road end at the Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center, about 578 ft. A park entrance pass is required, and overnight trips need an Olympic National Park wilderness permit booked in advance; the Hoh is a quota area.

pins.name: Hoh River Trailhead (Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center)

text: From US 101 about 13 miles south of Forks, turn east on the paved Upper Hoh Road and follow it about 18 miles to its end at the Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center. The park entrance fee applies; no Northwest Forest Pass is needed.

From US 101 about 13 miles south of Forks, turn east on Upper Hoh Road and drive about 18 miles to the road end at the Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center, about 578 ft. A park entrance pass is required, and overnight trips need an Olympic National Park wilderness permit booked in advance; the Hoh is a quota area.

Drive to the Upper Dungeness/Royal Basin Trailhead from Sequim by way of Palo Alto Road and Forest Roads 2880 and 2870; the trailhead is on FR 2870 and the hike starts on Trail #833.2. A Northwest Forest Pass is needed to park here. Royal Lake is an Olympic National Park quota area, so an overnight also requires a wilderness permit arranged in advance.
Drive to the Upper Dungeness Trailhead at the end of Forest Road 2870, at about 2,500 feet in Olympic National Forest. A Forest Service day-use pass is required at the trailhead.
Drive FR 2870 off Palo Alto Road to its end at the signed Baldy/Tyler Peak trailhead, a gravel pullout for about a dozen cars in the Upper Dungeness drainage of the Hood Canal Ranger District.

From US-101 near Sequim, follow Palo Alto Road to Lost Mountain Road (Forest Road 2870), then continue onto Forest Road 2860-120 and drive it to its end. The road stops at a dirt berm that blocks further vehicle travel, at roughly 3,300 feet, where there is room to park. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

From US 101 across from Sequim Bay State Park, turn west onto Louella Road and go about 0.9 mi, then turn left onto Palo Alto Road. Follow it about 6 mi as it becomes FS Road 28, turn right onto FS Road 2880 (steep, not suited to trailers), pass Dungeness Forks Campground, and stay left onto FS Road 2870 for about 12.5 mi to the Tubal Cain Trailhead at about 3,300 ft. A recreation pass such as the

pins.name: Index-Galena Road / North Fork Skykomish River Access (FR-63, ~Mile 10)

text: Drive US 2 to Skykomish, then head north on the Beckler River Road (FR-65) for about 15 miles and turn left (west) onto FR-63. A high-clearance vehicle is worth having for the last few miles. Park at the turnaround by the river crossing near Galena at about 1,150 feet; the pullout is unmarked and easy to drive past. No permits are needed, and the river here is the last dependable water, since ther

Follow the North Fork Skykomish River Road (FR 63) to its end at the Blanca Lake Trailhead, about 1,950 feet. This is a Forest Service fee site: pay the day-use fee at the kiosk or display a Northwest Forest or Interagency pass, as a Washington Discover Pass is not valid here. Check the North Fork road status before you drive out; road and trail are usually clear from early to mid summer through f

Obstruction Point Road is the way in, and it is the highest road in Olympic National Park: from the Hurricane Ridge Visitor Center follow it 8 miles east to its end at the Obstruction Point trailhead, topping out around 6,135 ft. It is narrow, one-lane gravel the whole way and no place for trailers. The road is usually open only from early-to-mid July through mid-October, so it is not a road you c

From Sultan, follow Sultan Basin Road north about 11.2 to 11.5 miles to the gated junction with Olney Creek Road. Olney Creek Road is closed to public vehicle travel, so that gate is where the drive ends. There is no formal lot — park on the road shoulder at the junction. The day starts on foot from the gate, walking the closed logging road uphill.

pins.name: Sol Duc Trailhead (end of Sol Duc Hot Springs Road)
Sol Duc Trailhead (Sol Duc Falls / Sol Duc River Trail, end of Sol Duc Hot Springs Rd)

text: From Port Angeles, drive west on US 101 about 29 miles, past Lake Crescent, and turn left onto Sol Duc Hot Springs Road. Follow it about 14 miles, past the hot springs resort, to the parking lot at the end of the road. A national park entrance pass is required, and overnight trips need an Olympic National Park wilderness permit.

Drive Sol Duc Hot Springs Road off US-101 and follow it about 13 to 14 miles past Sol Duc Hot Springs Resort, near Sol Duc Falls, to the road-end Sol Duc Trailhead in Olympic National Park. Any overnight stay needs a wilderness permit reserved in advance; none are issued at the trailhead. The trail is typically snow-free July through October. Do not plan on the Boulder Lake side instead: Olympic H

From Leavenworth take US-2 west 15 miles to Coles Corner, turn onto SR-207 (Lake Wenatchee Highway) for 10.5 miles, then follow White River Road/FS-6400 the final 10 miles to its end at the White River Trailhead, also called the Indian Creek Trailhead, at 2,300 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, and there is a self-issue wilderness permit at the kiosk. The Indian Creek Trail leaves from the

From US-2 at Coles Corner take WA-207 about ten miles up past Lake Wenatchee, then White River Road / FS-6400 another ten miles to the road end. Pavement gives out partway along; the gravel that follows is rough but not rutted, and the trailhead has a large gravelled lot shared with the Indian Creek, Mount David and PCT approaches.

From US 2 at Coles Corner, take SR 207 north toward Lake Wenatchee and continue onto White River Road (FS Road 6400), following it about 10 miles to its end at the White River Trailhead at 2,300 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.
Walk or bike the closed Olympic Hot Springs Road and then the Whiskey Bend Road, about 7 miles, to the Whiskey Bend Trailhead. Both roads are open to walkers and bicycles but not to vehicles.

From US-101 about 8 miles west of Port Angeles, turn south on Olympic Hot Springs Road into the Elwha Valley and drive to the Madison Falls parking area at the park boundary, where the road is closed to vehicles by flood damage. From there walk or bike the closed road and the Whiskey Bend Road, about 6 miles one way, to the trailhead. An Olympic National Park entrance pass applies, and overnight t

pins.name: Hurricane Ridge Visitor Center (High Ridge Trailhead)

text: Drive Hurricane Ridge Road about 17 miles south from Port Angeles — Race Street off Highway 101 — to the road's end at the Hurricane Ridge Visitor Center, around 5,250 ft. Park in the visitor center lot and start at its east end, on the paved Cirque Rim path onto the High Ridge Trail. Come early, since parking here fills. The seasonal contact station has restrooms and potable water, and it is the

From US-97A at Entiat, turn onto Entiat River Road (County Road 19, which becomes FS Road 51) and drive about 32 miles up the valley, then turn right onto FS Road 5606, about two miles past Silver Falls Campground. Follow FS Road 5606 about 3 miles to its end at the North Fork Entiat Trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

From US 97A at Entiat, turn onto Entiat River Road (County Road 19, which becomes FR 51) just after the bridge and drive about 32 miles up the valley to FR 5606, about 2 miles past Silver Falls Campground. Follow FR 5606 north about 3 miles to its end at the North Fork Entiat Trailhead, about 3,940 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or the day-use fee is required.

From US-97A at Entiat, turn onto Entiat River Road (County Road 19, which becomes FS Road 51) and drive about 32 miles up the valley, then turn right onto FS Road 5606, about two miles past Silver Falls Campground. Follow FS Road 5606 about 3 miles to its end at the North Fork Entiat Trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

From US 97A at Entiat, turn onto Entiat River Road (County Road 19, which becomes FR 51) and drive 32.3 miles to FR 5606; if you reach North Fork Campground you have gone too far. Follow FR 5606 for 3 miles to the road end at about 3,900 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free Glacier Peak Wilderness permit is self-issued at the kiosk.

Drive the Entiat River Road (FR 51) to its end at the Cottonwood Camp trailhead. Early in the season the road can be gated or still snowed in below the trailhead, which adds several miles of road walking or biking before the trail even starts — confirm access before committing to the drive.

From Granite Falls, drive the Mountain Loop Highway east about 27 to 28 miles, then turn onto Sunrise Mine Road, Forest Road 4065. Follow roughly 2.3 to 2.5 miles of gravel to the road's end at the Sunrise Mine Trailhead, where Trail No. 707 starts. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

From Granite Falls, drive the Mountain Loop Highway east about 28 mi (about 17 mi past the Verlot Public Service Center) and turn right on Sunrise Mine Road (FS Road 4065). Follow this rough gravel road about 2.3 mi to its end at the Sunrise Mine Trailhead, at about 2,350 ft. High clearance is recommended, and a Northwest Forest Pass is required.

From Granite Falls, drive the Mountain Loop Highway east about 28 miles and turn right onto Sunrise Mine Road (FR 4065), marked by small signs. Follow the gravel about 2.3 miles to its end at the Sunrise Mine Trailhead, around 2,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

From Granite Falls, drive the Mountain Loop Highway east about 28 miles and turn right onto Sunrise Mine Road (FS Road 4065). Follow the gravel road about 2.3 miles to its end at the Sunrise Mine Trailhead, about 2,350 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

The trailhead is at Barlow Pass, at the end of the paved Mountain Loop Highway, where a gate blocks the old Monte Cristo Road. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and there is a self-issue wilderness permit kiosk at the gate before you start up the closed roadbed. The road and its river bridges beyond the gate are washed out, so nearly every current party bikes or hikes the first four-plu

From Granite Falls, follow the Mountain Loop Highway east about 31 miles to Barlow Pass, where the pavement ends, and park at the trailhead lot at about 2,360 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is required.

pins.name: Little Giant Trailhead (Chiwawa River Road, Trail #1518)

text: From US 2 at Coles Corner, take SR 207 north 4.4 miles, turn right on Chiwawa Loop Road for 0.4 mile, then take the second left onto Chiwawa River Road (FS Road 62) and drive about 19 miles to the Little Giant Trailhead at 2,600 ft. The road turns to rough gravel and dirt after about 11 miles. No parking pass is needed; fill out the free wilderness permit at the trailhead.

Barlow Pass is where the pavement ends on the Mountain Loop Highway. The old Monte Cristo road beyond the gate is closed to cars but open to bikes, and most parties ride it to save their legs for the scramble.
